title: Riverbend Clinic real-world triage eval notes
body:
Context:
- Customer: Riverbend Clinic (regional outpatient network, primary & urgent care).
- Goal: prototype an asynchronous clinician triage assistant that summarizes patient-submitted intake notes (free text + attachments) and suggests urgency category + recommended intake routing.
- Constraint: PHI must not leave customer VPC; audit logs + KMS-managed keys required.

High-level ask from last call (2024-11-05):
- Need an on-prem/VPC deployment that can:
  - Accept JSON payloads from their form pipeline (avg 350 tokens, P95 2,500 tokens with attachments OCR).
  - Return structured JSON: {urgency_level, summary, red_flags[], recommended_action}.
  - SLA: 99th perc latency target ~ 800ms for single-request (soft), throughput target 80 req/min sustained.
  - Retention: logs for 30 days, audit trail for 1 year (redacted tokens acceptable).

Technical notes & gotchas observed during feasibility:
- Tokenization/length: many real patient notes include long quoted histories; propose client-side pre-chunking + prefix context. If we pass raw 2,500-token docs to a 4k context model, costs spike. Consider summarization microservice to compress prior to LLM.
- OCR attachments: noisy text increases hallucination risk. Need deterministic extraction + simple heuristics (e.g., date detection, DOB normalization) before prompt.
- Structured outputs: function-calling or strict JSON schema is preferred. Recommend we implement Redwood console schema-validation hook + fallback to pattern match.
- PHI handling: must ensure KV cache isn't persisted outside VPC. Confirm: Redwood Private supports customer-managed storage for KV; need to verify with infra.
- Model variants: start with a smaller open medical-tuned model (quantized) for cost, fallback to larger for high-urgency or low-confidence. Need to define confidence threshold.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated patient follow-ups could help, but for PHI we must encrypt caches & control TTLs.

Operational & security items:
- KMS: Riverbend uses Azure Key Vault; confirm Redwood Private can integrate with AKV via our KMS connector.
- Audit logs: they want per-request hash + redaction. Plan: hash IDs at edge, store redacted trace in customer S3 inside VPC.
- RBAC: clinicians vs admin access to console; they prefer SSO via Okta.

Prompting sketch (initial):
- System: "You are a clinical triage assistant. Use only the supplied patient text and attachments metadata. Output JSON with keys: urgency_level (low/medium/high), concise_summary (<= 40 words), red_flags (list), recommended_action (one of: schedule-televisit, urgent-visit, send-to-ER, no-action). If unsure, set urgency_level to 'medium' and include 'requires human review' in recommended_action."
- User input: raw_notes + structured fields (age, meds, allergies).
- Safety: explicit instruction to not guess diagnoses, only surface red flags and routing.

Evaluation ideas (real-world):
- Build a small evaluation harness: sample 200 de-identified real intake forms (already anonymized by Riverbend data team). Metrics: precision/recall on red_flags, exact match on recommended_action, summary ROUGE-L vs clinician summary, latency distribution.
- Regression alerts: tie to Redwood Optimize — alert when red_flag recall drops > 8% vs baseline.

Cost sketch (very rough):
- Expectation: using a quantized local 13B variant for baseline. Token cost roughly equivalent to $0.002 / 1k tokens infra when on dedicated; rough monthly delta depends on utilization.
- For 80 req/min sustained with avg 600 tokens/request = ~28.8M tokens/day -> need dedicated capacity.
- We should produce a dedicated capacity sizing spreadsheet for next sync.

Open questions to resolve with Riverbend: (assignments)
- (Jonas) Confirm exact retention policy for raw text vs redacted logs. Needed by 2024-11-14.
- (Priya) Validate Azure Key Vault tenant + service principal details for KMS integration. Needed by 2024-11-12.
- (Amira) Collect 200 de-id examples + clinician triage labels for eval. Target: 2024-11-20.
- (Infra) Can Redwood Private disable external kernel telemetry for their cluster? (ask infra team).

Immediate next steps (internal):
- Draft a minimal POC architecture diagram (edge -> preprocessor -> Redwood Private inference pool -> redaction/audit store in VPC). Due 2024-11-09. (Priya)
- Prepare a short cost/throughput spreadsheet with 3 scenarios (POC, pilot 1K users/day, production 10K+ users/day). Due 2024-11-13. (Jonas)
- Build a prototype prompt + function schema in local sandbox, test on 20 de-id samples to sanity-check classification mapping. (Amira)

Notes to mention on next customer touchpoint:
- Emphasize we can route high-confidence traffic to cheaper quantized models and auto-fallback to higher-capacity instances for high-urgency hits.
- Ask about exact ER routing requirements (do they want auto-flag to phone tree? immediate EHR ticket?).
- Clarify whether they require synchronous attachments processing or async callback (suggest async for large OCRs).

Quick checklist before demo v0:
- [ ] Confirm KMS/Azure details
- [ ] Collect de-id sample set
- [ ] POC architecture diagram + security slide
- [ ] Minimal Redwood Private instance spin (sandbox) + test schema
- [ ] Simple latency runbook for clinicians

Random observations from call:
- Clinician was very worried about hallucinations from OCR noise — we should show a failure-mode slide.
- They use a legacy EHR with a nightly batch ingest; consider a nightly bulk evaluation to measure drift.

Reference snippets to include in follow-up email:
- "We recommend a two-stage pipeline: 1) lightweight normalization & compression (summarizer) running in VPC; 2) structured triage model with JSON schema enforcement and audit logs. This reduces per-request cost and improves guardrails."

End notes:
- This doc is a working scratchpad — will formalize into a customer-facing proposal once we have KMS confirmation and sample data.
body_summary: Call notes and action items for Riverbend Clinic triage assistant POC covering PHI constraints, VPC/KMS requirements, tokenization and OCR gotchas, model fallback strategy, evaluation plan, approximate capacity/cost sketch, and immediate next steps with owners and due dates.
